subject: Information Theory
title: The Enigma Machine
description: A quick, practical guide to The Enigma Machine.

hook.text: Germany's Enigma had 158 trillion possible settings. The Allies broke it anyway, shortening WWII by years.

buildup.text: Enigma used rotating wheels that changed the substitution with every keypress, defeating simple frequency analysis.

discovery.text: Polish mathematicians found structural weaknesses. Turing built machines to exploit repeated patterns.

twist.text: The fatal flaw: Enigma never encrypted a letter as itself. That single rule gave codebreakers a foothold.

climax.text: Breaking Enigma showed that complexity alone isn't security. Structural flaws can undo any machine.

punchline.text: One design rule. One fatal weakness.

quiz.question: What structural flaw helped break Enigma?
options: A letter could never encrypt as itself
